025.name: Marriage Resignation
025.hitokoto: A 1966 ruling voided marriage resignation, 20 years before the statute did.
body: Company rules requiring women to resign on marriage were voided in court before they were voided by statute. Sumitomo Cement had women submit, on hiring, a written undertaking to "resign on marriage or on reaching the full age of 35", but the Tokyo District Court judgment of 20 December 1966 held the marriage resignation rule void, as a restriction on freedom to marry and discrimination by sex.

What cut the ground from under the rule was the Equal Employment Opportunity Act. Promulgated on 1 June 1985 (Act No. 45 of 1985) and in force from 1 April 1986, it forbade from enactment in 1985 both discrimination by sex in retirement age and dismissal and any provision making marriage, pregnancy or childbirth a ground for resignation (Article 11); the 1997 amendment (in force April 1999) turned discrimination by sex in recruitment and hiring, and in assignment and promotion, from a duty to endeavour into a prohibition. "Marriage resignation" appears in the record of Diet proceedings from 1964, but the word kotobuki taisha first appears in October 2001.

The curve of the practice can be followed in the National Fertility Survey. The share of wives who were working when they decided to marry and were out of work immediately after it fell from 37.3% for marriages of 1985-89 to 25.1% for 2000-04 and to 14.0% for 2015-19, while continuing in work across marriage reached 79.8%. When the word kotobuki taisha was born could not be confirmed from the dictionaries.

made.label: Showa The marriage resignation rule
made.fact: The first appearance of the word kotobuki taisha could not be fixed from the dictionaries or the record of Diet proceedings (in the Diet record the first is 26 October 2001, House of Representatives Committee on Health, Labour and Welfare, Tomoko Nakagawa). The marriage resignation rule itself was common enough to be litigated in the 1960s: Sumitomo Cement had women submit, on hiring, a written undertaking to "resign on marriage or on reaching the full age of 35". "Marriage resignation" first appears in the Diet record on 3 December 1964 (House of Councillors Committee on Social and Labour Affairs).

discontinued.label: 1966 Marriage resignation void
discontinued.fact: 20 December 1966: the Tokyo District Court (the Sumitomo Cement case, Rominshu vol. 17 no. 6 p. 1407) held a marriage resignation rule applying to women only void, as a restriction on freedom to marry and discriminatory treatment by sex. The Equal Employment Opportunity Act (Act No. 45 of 1 June 1985, in force 1 April 1986) cut the ground from under the rule, forbidding in Article 11 as enacted discrimination by sex in retirement age and dismissal and provisions making marriage and the like a ground for resignation; the 1997 amendment (Act No. 92 of 18 June 1997, in force 1 April 1999) made discrimination by sex in recruitment and hiring, and in assignment and promotion, a prohibition too.

keyfacts.text: The Sumitomo Cement case: filed in 1964, judgment of the Tokyo District Court on 20 December 1966. The company had women submit on hiring a written undertaking to "resign on marriage or on reaching the full age of 35", and dismissed a woman employee who did not resign after marrying; the judgment held the marriage resignation rule void as contrary to public order and good morals, and ordered confirmation of her status under the employment contract and payment of unpaid wages.

The Equal Employment Opportunity Act was promulgated on 1 June 1985 (Act No. 45 of 1985) as an amendment to the Working Women's Welfare Act (Act No. 113 of 1972), and came into force on 1 April 1986 under Article 1 of its supplementary provisions.

The 16th National Fertility Survey, figure 9-1-2: the share of "marriage resignation" wives, who were working when they decided to marry and out of work immediately after it, was 37.3% for marriages of 1985-89, 34.5% for 1990-94, 31.2% for 1995-99, 25.1% for 2000-04, 24.1% for 2005-09, 17.6% for 2010-14 and 14.0% for 2015-19. Continuing in work rose from 56.6% to 79.8%.

The rate at which wives who had been working before pregnancy continued in work across the birth of a first child rose from 57.7% for first births in 2010-14 to 69.5% in 2015-19, and 79.2% of those who continued used the childcare leave system.

In the record of Diet proceedings "marriage resignation" appears from the House of Councillors Committee on Social and Labour Affairs of 3 December 1964, with 239 instances to September 2026. The first appearance of kotobuki taisha is the House of Representatives Committee on Health, Labour and Welfare of 26 October 2001, with 33 in all to September 2026.

curve.subtitle: So-called "marriage resignation". ◆By year of marriage; the horizontal axis is the middle year of each five-year band.

026.name: Three Years on a Rock
026.reading: ishi no ue ni mo sannen
026.hitokoto: More of the 2004 graduates quit within three years than of the 2022 graduates.
body: "Three years on a rock" is a proverb current since the early Edo period. The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten, concise edition, gives as its first appearance the haikai collection Kefukigusa (1638), and Saikaku oridome (1694) has "three years on a rock, as the common saying has it". There is no settled account of its origin, and the reading that ties it to Bodhidharma's nine years facing a wall is not taken up by the dictionaries.

Evidence that the proverb has fallen out of use is, unexpectedly, absent from the statistics. In the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's tabulation, the share of new university graduates leaving their job within three years begins at 28.4% for those graduating in March 1987; the lowest is 23.7% for 1992 graduates, the highest 36.6% for 2004, and 2022 graduates are at 33.8%. It rose from the middle 20s in the early 1990s to the 30s in the middle of that decade, and has run a little above 30% since.

Job changers numbered 3.51 million in 2019 (3.53 million in the figures adjusted for the time series), the most since 2002, and stand high at 3.31 million in 2024 and 3.30 million in 2025, but that is a movement of the whole workforce, the middle-aged included. The story that more young people fail to keep to "three years" is not borne out by the three-year separation rate for university graduates, at least not from the 2000s on.

made.label: 1638 Kefukigusa
made.fact: The dictionaries give as its first appearance the haikai collection Kefukigusa (1638), and volume four of the ukiyozoshi Saikaku oridome (1694) has "merchant or artisan, do not change the place you have grown used to; three years on a rock, as the common saying has it". In the early Edo period the form was "sit three years on a rock and it warms", and the second half was later dropped. There is no settled account of its origin.

keyfacts.text: The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten, concise edition, and others: the first appearance is the haikai collection Kefukigusa (1638), and Saikaku oridome (1694) has "three years on a rock, as the common saying has it". The reading that ties it to Bodhidharma's nine years facing a wall is not taken up by the dictionaries and is not the settled view.

Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, "Job Separation of New School Graduates", appendix 1: the rate of leaving within three years of starting work, for university graduates, was 28.4% for those graduating in March 1987, 23.7% for 1992 graduates (the lowest), 36.5% for 2000, 36.6% for 2004 (the highest), 28.8% for 2009, 32.3% for 2020, 34.9% for 2021 and 33.8% for 2022.

Statistics Bureau of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Labour Force Survey (Detailed Tabulation): job changers peaked at 3.46 million in 2006 and 2007, fell after the Lehman shock, rose from 2011, and reached 3.51 million in 2019, the most since 2002, the first year comparable. 2024 was about 3.31 million, a third straight rise.
In JILPT's 8th Survey on Working Life (2021), 82.0% supported "staying with one company until retirement age".
In the record of Diet proceedings "three years on a rock" is quoted only as a proverb, and is no index of the rise or fall of the norm.

027.name: Fight 24 Hours?
027.hitokoto: The same jingle was sung again 25 years later, as "24 hours is too hard".
body: Sankyo's energy drink Regain went on sale in June 1988, and at the end of May 1989 came the commercial in which Ushiwakamaru Saburota, played by Saburo Tokito, sings 24-jikan tatakaemasu ka ("Can you fight for 24 hours?"). The jingle Yuki no shirushi ("Sign of Courage") was released as a single on 22 November that year, and the phrase took the bronze prize in the buzzword division of the 6th New Words and Buzzwords Award for 1989. The copy itself dates from the launch in 1988, and the month the craze caught can be fixed.

The lapse can be followed by date too. In 1991, after the bubble burst, the copy was changed to 24-jikan, tatakau anata ni ("For you, fighting 24 hours"), and the copy and the song came back once with Regain 24 in 2007; then on 1 July 2014 a commercial for Suntory Beverage & Food's Regain Energy Drink sang the same song again as 24-jikan tatakau no wa shindoi ("Fighting 24 hours is rough"), with the copy 3, 4-jikan tatakaemasu ka ("Can you fight for three or four hours?"). In 2018 a manager at Daiichi Sankyo Healthcare said it "has become a dead word".

The law moved the same way. Under the Work Style Reform Act, in force from 1 April 2019, the cap on overtime was set at 45 hours a month and 360 hours a year as a rule, and came to carry a penalty (1 April 2020 for small and medium firms). The new Regain product released in February 2019 was pitched at the "age of the hundred-year life". The norm of fighting 24 hours had its contents swapped while the product name stayed.

made.label: 1989 The Regain commercial
made.fact: Sankyo's energy drink Regain went on sale in June 1988. The commercial Yuki no shirushi ("Sign of Courage"), in which Saburo Tokito, as Ushiwakamaru Saburota, sings 24-jikan tatakaemasu ka ("Can you fight for 24 hours?"), began broadcasting at the end of May 1989, and the single Yuki no shirushi: Regain no thema was released on 22 November 1989. It took the bronze prize in the buzzword division of the 6th New Words and Buzzwords Award the same year.

discontinued.label: 2014 The "three or four hours" ad
discontinued.fact: On 1 July 2014 the commercial for Suntory Beverage & Food's carbonated drink Regain Energy Drink (featuring Sumire, sung by Makoto Kawamoto) sang the same song again as 24-jikan tatakau no wa shindoi ("Fighting 24 hours is rough") and made the copy 3, 4-jikan tatakaemasu ka ("Can you fight for three or four hours?"). Under the Work Style Reform Act, in force from 1 April 2019, the cap on overtime (45 hours a month and 360 hours a year as a rule) came to carry a penalty (1 April 2020 for small and medium firms).

keyfacts.text: Regain went on sale from Sankyo in 1988 (June). From the end of May 1989 commercials using Yuki no shirushi began, and the single CD was released in November that year. At the 6th New Words and Buzzwords Award for 1989, "24-JIKAN TATAKAEMASU KA" took the bronze prize in the buzzword division.

In 1991, after the bubble burst, the catchphrase was changed to 24-jikan, tatakau anata ni ("For you, fighting 24 hours"). In 2018 Masaaki Hanawa of the product strategy department of Daiichi Sankyo Healthcare said that "'24-jikan tatakaemasu ka' has become a dead word".

On 1 July 2014, in the television commercial for Regain Energy Drink released by Suntory, Sumire appeared as a live-action Lum, with the lyric 24-jikan tatakau no wa shindoi ("Fighting 24 hours is rough") over an arrangement of Yuki no shirushi sung by Makoto Kawamoto, and the catchphrase became 3, 4-jikan tatakaemasu ka? ("Can you fight for three or four hours?").

I'm, a group company of Daiichi Sankyo Healthcare, released Regain Triple Force (a quasi-drug, 60 tablets, 4,200 yen) on 27 February 2019, turning from "Can you fight for 24 hours?" to "health first" and "recovering youthfulness" (WWD JAPAN, 5 December 2018).

The cap on overtime under the Work Style Reform Act came into force on 1 April 2019 for large firms and 1 April 2020 for small and medium ones. The cap is 45 hours a month and 360 hours a year as a rule; even under a special clause, within 720 hours a year, an average of 80 hours over any several months, under 100 hours in a month, and above 45 hours in no more than six months a year. Breach carries imprisonment of up to six months (imprisonment with labour until May 2025) or a fine of up to 300,000 yen.
In the record of Diet proceedings, "can you fight for 24 hours" first appears on 15 June 1990 (Special Committee on Disaster Countermeasures, Seiichiro Murakami), with nine instances in all.

028.name: Guts
028.hitokoto: Konjo was a Buddhist term. Sports konjo is held to date from the 1964 Olympics.
body: Konjo was originally a Buddhist term, for the capacity of one who receives the Buddha's teaching. It became a doctrine of spirit in sport after the war, and the time can be fixed. Hirofumi Daimatsu, coach of Nichibo Kaizuka, published Ore ni tsuite koi! Watashi no shobu konjo ("Follow Me! My Fighting Guts") in June 1963, and at the Tokyo Olympics of October 1964 the "Oriental Witches" took the gold medal. The oldest instance of the word konjoron in the record of Diet proceedings is "I am in favour of the doctrine of guts", said by the Director-General of the Defence Agency at the House of Councillors Budget Committee of 19 March 1969.

Yusuke Okabe's The Birth and Transformation of the Doctrine of Guts in Sport (Junposha, 2021) argues that the doctrine took shape around the Tokyo Olympics of 1964 and settled in as a view of sport that put victory above all. Hideto Suzuki reads Daimatsu's idea of coaching as the making of a thought out of the "war experience" of surviving the Imphal campaign (Japan Journal of Physical Education, Health and Sport Sciences, vol. 66, 2021). Star of the Giants (Weekly Shonen Magazine, no. 19 of 1966 to no. 3 of 1971) made the mould of supokon.

There is no date of lapse, but there is a turning point. On 23 December 2012 the captain of the basketball team at Sakuranomiya High School in Osaka killed himself over corporal punishment by his teacher-coach, and the coach was convicted at the Osaka District Court on 26 September 2013. In March 2018 the guidelines of the Japan Sports Agency set at least two rest days a week and stated that corporal punishment "is not permitted in any case". Guts remain, but the way of it, training without rest and under blows, was denied again, this time from the side of the institutions.

made.label: 1964 The Tokyo Olympics
made.fact: Hirofumi Daimatsu's Ore ni tsuite koi! Watashi no shobu konjo ("Follow Me! My Fighting Guts") was published in June 1963 in the Kodansha How-To Books series (238 pages), and at the Tokyo Olympics of October 1964 Daimatsu's Japan women's volleyball team, the "Oriental Witches", took the gold medal. Yusuke Okabe argues that the "doctrine of guts in sport" took shape around the Tokyo Olympics of 1964. The oldest instance of the word konjoron in the record of Diet proceedings is the House of Councillors Budget Committee of 19 March 1969 (Kiichi Arita, Director-General of the Defence Agency: "I am in favour of the doctrine of guts").

keyfacts.text: Hirofumi Daimatsu's Ore ni tsuite koi! Watashi no shobu konjo was published in June 1963 in the Kodansha How-To Books series (238 pages). The sequel, Naseba naru! Zoku ore ni tsuite koi, appeared in 1964.

Hirofumi Daimatsu (12 February 1921 to 24 November 1978) became coach of Nichibo Kaizuka in 1954, beat the Soviet Union to win the world championship in 1962, and led the Japan women's team to the gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics of 1964. Hideto Suzuki analyses his idea of coaching as the making of a thought out of the "war experience" of surviving the Imphal campaign.

Yusuke Okabe's The Birth and Transformation of the Doctrine of Guts in Sport: The Will to Excellence, the Pursuit of Victory (Junposha, November 2021) argues that the doctrine of guts in sport took shape around the Tokyo Olympics of 1964 and thereafter settled in as a view of sport that put victory above all.
Star of the Giants (story by Ikki Kajiwara, art by Noboru Kawasaki) ran in Weekly Shonen Magazine from no. 19 of 1966 to no. 3 of 1971, and is held to be the first of the supokon baseball comics.

On 23 December 2012 the captain (aged 17) of the basketball team at Sakuranomiya High School in Osaka killed himself over corporal punishment by his teacher-coach. The coach was dismissed for misconduct on 12 February 2013 and, on 26 September 2013, given one year's imprisonment suspended for three years by the Osaka District Court for assault and bodily injury. On 24 February 2016 the Tokyo District Court found a causal link between the corporal punishment and the suicide and ordered the City of Osaka to pay about 75 million yen in damages.

The Japan Sports Agency's "Comprehensive Guidelines on Extracurricular Athletic Club Activities" (March 2018) set at least two rest days a week during term (at least one weekday and at least one weekend day), and held corporal punishment to be "not permitted in any case".

curve.title: Speeches in the record of Diet proceedings ◆containing the word konjo
curve.note: Counted year by year as the number of speeches containing the word in the National Diet Proceedings Search System. The record for the most recent years comes in late, so the chart runs to 2024.
curve.subtitle: Includes uses other than the doctrine of guts, such as shimaguni konjo, "island mentality". ◆To 2024

029.name: Nominication
029.hitokoto: In Nippon Life's survey, "unnecessary" first became the majority in 2021.
body: The coinage joining nomi, drinking, to "communication" is oldest, in the National Diet Library's index of magazine articles, in "A History of Nominication" in Ushio for August 1982, and the spelling with the character for drinking goes back to Gekkan Somu for November 1983. In the Diet, a witness said "communication, nominication" at the House of Representatives Committee on Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on 23 April 1992. It spread as a name for the workplace culture of the late Showa period.

In the survey on Labour Thanksgiving Day that Nippon Life has published each November since 2017, those calling nominication at work "necessary" were 62.0% in 2017, 53.6% in 2018, 57.3% in 2019 and 54.3% in 2020. In 2021 (1-13 October, 7,774 respondents) it fell to 38.2%, and "unnecessary" at 61.9% was the higher for the first time since the survey began. It has stayed in the 40s since: 45.6% in 2022, 44.7% in 2023, 43.5% in 2024.

In the surveys of 2023 and 2024, about seven in ten said they did not want to work at a place with nominication (67.4% and 70.2%). Meanwhile 34.1% had had nominication in fiscal 2023, back up from 14.3% the year before, so the drinking itself has not gone. What has fallen is the share who think it necessary.

made.label: 1982 First in the magazine index
made.fact: The oldest article containing nominikeshon in NDL Search (the index of magazine articles) is "Sansuijin suikyo mondo 8: A History of Nominication" in Ushio for August 1982; the oldest with the spelling using the character for drinking is Gekkan Somu for November 1983, and for nomyunikeshon, Senken Romu Kanri for November 1983. There are no hits before 1980. In the record of Diet proceedings, "communication, nominication" appears at the House of Representatives Committee on Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on 23 April 1992 (witness Ryuzo Kigasawa), and the spelling with the character for drinking at the House of Councillors Committee on Audit on 2 September 1994 (Arinobu Morizumi).

keyfacts.text: In Nippon Life's "Nissay Internet Survey: On Labour Thanksgiving Day" for 2021 (surveyed 1-13 October, 7,774 respondents, announced 17 November), those answering that nominication at work was "necessary" or "rather necessary" were 38.2% (down 16.1 points on the year), and "unnecessary" or "rather unnecessary" 61.9%. For the first time since the survey began in 2017, unnecessary was higher than necessary.

The "necessary" share over time in the same survey: 62.0% in 2017 (5,901 respondents), 53.6% in 2018 (8,021), 57.3% in 2019 (4,644), 54.3% in 2020 (25,062). From 2017 to 2019 the question offered necessary or unnecessary; from 2020 it offered four options, and the figure is "necessary" plus "rather necessary".

2022 (9,553 respondents) was 45.6% (up 7.4 points on the year), 2023 (7,400) 44.7% against 55.2% unnecessary, and 2024 (8,953) 43.5% against 56.4%. In both 2023 and 2024 about seven in ten (67.4% and 70.2%) answered that they did not want to work at a place with nominication.

Those who had "had nominication with people from work" in fiscal 2023 were 34.1%, a sharp rise from 14.3% in fiscal 2022. In the 2024 survey, those saying the frequency had "risen compared with last year" were 12.2%, half the 24.3% of the year before. The drinking itself has come back, but the side that thinks it necessary is still in the 40s.

First appearances of the word: in the NDL index of magazine articles, "A History of Nominication" in Ushio for August 1982 is the oldest. The spelling with the character for drinking dates from Gekkan Somu for November 1983. In the record of Diet proceedings the first appearances are 23 April 1992 (in katakana) and 2 September 1994 (with the character for drinking).

curve.title: Share answering that nominication at work ◆is necessary
curve.subtitle: "Necessary" plus "rather necessary"

030.name: Aim for Number One
030.hitokoto: "You need not be No. 1" sold 3.14 million copies and became No. 1.
body: Shito goraku is a phrase about how long a candidate sleeps: four hours and you pass, five and you fail. It comes from the pre-war election phrase "X to pass, Y to fail" (a newspaper of the 1930s has go-to san-raku, 50,000 yen to win and 30,000 to lose), and its transfer to entrance examinations is found in use from about the end of the 1950s. The norm of aiming for number one circulated in quantity in the 1960s, when the phrase "examination war" settled into the press.

The answer to it came out on 5 March 2003. SMAP's Sekai ni hitotsu dake no hana ("The Only Flower in the World"), written and composed by Noriyuki Makihara, sings "You need not be No. 1; you were always a special Only one"; it passed two million on 4 August that year and three million on 19 December 2016, and at 3.140 million copies in all became the biggest single of the Heisei era. The "yutori" Course of Study, which cut the content taught by about 30%, had come into effect in primary and lower secondary schools in April 2002, the year before.

"Crossing the finish line hand in hand at sports day" has been told and retold in the Diet as the emblem of this turn. It was mentioned as a case in Hiroshima Prefecture at the House of Councillors Committee on Education, Culture and Science on 24 September 1998, and at the House of Councillors Special Committee on the Basic Act on Education on 22 November 2006 Prime Minister Shinzo Abe said that "it was in fact being done"; the same day, however, Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasuhisa Shiozaki answered that "I have never myself seen anyone cross the line hand in hand on the spot, though I have heard the story in various places". No survey showing where and how much it was done was found within what this catalogue looked at.

made.label: Late 1950s The examination race
made.fact: Shito goraku, on how long a candidate sleeps (four hours and you pass, five and you fail), is found in use from about the end of the 1950s. Its origin is the pre-war election phrase "X to pass, Y to fail"; a newspaper of the 1930s has go-to san-raku, 50,000 yen to win and 30,000 to lose.

keyfacts.text: Shito goraku is found in use as an examination phrase from the end of the 1950s, transferred from the pre-war election phrase "X to pass, Y to fail". The writer at Kanji Cafe (2020) notes that cutting sleep dulls the head instead, so it is probably out of fashion now.

SMAP's Sekai ni hitotsu dake no hana (written and composed by Noriyuki Makihara) was released on 5 March 2003 as their 35th single. The lyric runs "You need not be No. 1; you were always a special Only one". It passed two million in its 21st week, on 4 August 2003, and three million on 19 December 2016; at 3.140 million copies in all (as at 27 January 2025) it is the biggest single of the Heisei era. It was first on Oricon's annual chart for 2003.

The Course of Study announced in December 1998 for primary and lower secondary schools, which cut the content taught by about 30% and set out "zest for living", came into effect from April 2002, as did the full five-day school week. The 2008 revision turned away from yutori, phased in from 2011.

"Crossing the finish line hand in hand at sports day" is recorded in the proceedings of the Diet. At the House of Councillors Committee on Education, Culture and Science on 24 September 1998, Noriko Hayashi said, of primary schools in Miyoshi, Shobara and Fukuyama in Hiroshima Prefecture, that "to rank people first and second is discrimination; let us all cross the line together hand in hand". At the House of Councillors Special Committee on the Basic Act on Education on 22 November 2006, Prime Minister Shinzo Abe said "it was in fact being done", while Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasuhisa Shiozaki answered that "I have never myself seen anyone cross the line hand in hand on the spot".

031.name: Own Your Home
031.hitokoto: Home ownership has held at 60% for 50 years. What fell is belief in land.
body: The view of life that takes owning a home as proof of being a full adult was established together with post-war housing policy. Under the Government Housing Loan Corporation Act (Act No. 156 of 6 May 1950) the corporation opened on 5 June that year; with the Public Housing Act (Act No. 193 of 4 June 1951) and the Japan Housing Corporation Act (Act No. 53 of 8 July 1955) the three pillars of loans, public housing and the housing corporation were in place, and the Housing Construction Planning Act (Act No. 100 of 30 June 1966) bound them into five-year plans. The housing construction five-year plans ran from the first to the eighth, fiscal 1966 to 2005.

The home ownership rate itself, however, has not fallen. In the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' Housing and Land Survey it was 59.2% in 1973 and 60.9% in 2023, flat at about 60% for half a century. What fell is on the side of attitudes. In the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism's Public Opinion Survey on Land Issues, those who think "land is a more advantageous asset than savings or shares" fell from 61.8% in fiscal 1993 to 37.0% in fiscal 1998, 27.1% in fiscal 2019 and 21.8% in fiscal 2023 (by post from fiscal 2020).

"I want to own both the land and the building" also fell, from 83.3% in fiscal 1993 to 73.5% in fiscal 2019 and 65.0% in fiscal 2023, taken by post. On the side of the institutions, the Basic Act for Housing (Act No. 61 of 8 June 2006) repealed the Housing Construction Planning Act, and the Government Housing Loan Corporation too was abolished on 31 March 2007, its business passing to the Japan Housing Finance Agency. The policy of building quantity is over, and the owned home is returning from an "advantageous asset" to a place to live.

made.label: 1950 The Housing Loan Corporation
made.fact: The Government Housing Loan Corporation was established on 5 June 1950 under the Government Housing Loan Corporation Act (Act No. 156 of 6 May 1950). With the Japan Housing Corporation Act (Act No. 53 of 8 July 1955) and the Housing Construction Planning Act (Act No. 100 of 30 June 1966), the three pillars of the corporation's loans for owned homes, the housing corporation and public housing were in place, and the housing construction five-year plans ran from the first (fiscal 1966) to the eighth (to fiscal 2005).

discontinued.label: 2007 The corporation abolished
discontinued.fact: The Basic Act for Housing (Act No. 61 of 8 June 2006, in force the same day) repealed the Housing Construction Planning Act, and the housing construction five-year plans ended with the eighth (fiscal 2005). The Government Housing Loan Corporation was abolished on 31 March 2007, its business passing on 1 April 2007 to the Japan Housing Finance Agency, an incorporated administrative agency. The institutional end point of the "policy of owned homes by quantity".

keyfacts.text: The Government Housing Loan Corporation Act is Act No. 156 of 6 May 1950, the Japan Housing Corporation Act is Act No. 53 of 8 July 1955, and the Housing Construction Planning Act is Act No. 100 of 30 June 1966.

The home ownership rate in the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' Housing and Land Survey was 59.2% in 1973 and 60.9% in 2023 (rented 35.0%), flat at about 60% for half a century. The "fall" is not a matter of the ownership rate.

In the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism's Public Opinion Survey on Land Issues, those answering "I think land is a more advantageous asset than savings or shares and the like" went 61.8% in fiscal 1993, 37.0% in fiscal 1998, 39.3% in fiscal 2008, 27.1% in fiscal 2019, 21.5% in fiscal 2020, 17.4% in fiscal 2021, 17.9% in fiscal 2022 and 21.8% in fiscal 2023. From fiscal 2020 the method changed from interview to post, so the ministry does not compare simply with earlier years.

In the same survey, "as for land and building, I want to own both" went 83.3% in fiscal 1993, 79.2% in fiscal 2000, 80.9% in fiscal 2010, 75.7% in fiscal 2017, 73.5% in fiscal 2019 and 65.0% in fiscal 2023. "Renting is fine" went from 9.4% to 17.5%.

The Basic Act for Housing is Act No. 61 of 8 June 2006 (in force the same day). The Government Housing Loan Corporation was abolished on 31 March 2007 and its business passed to the Japan Housing Finance Agency on 1 April.

curve.title: Those who think land an advantageous asset, ◆and the home ownership rate
curve.subtitle: The question is "land is a more advantageous asset than savings or shares"

032.name: Credentialism
032.hitokoto: Thirty-odd years after "no credentials asked", university entry is at a record.
body: The phrase gakureki shakai, "credential society", came into wide use from around the start of the 1960s (Heibonsha World Encyclopedia). It was a period in which the rate of going on to university kept rising, and the OECD education mission that came to Japan in January 1970, Johan Galtung among them, noted in its report that entry to university was decided by a single examination taken at 18. Criticism concentrates in the second half of the 1970s: Makoto Aso and Morikazu Ushiogi, eds., On the Utility of Credentials (Yuhikaku, 1977), and Ushiogi's The Turn of the Credential Society (University of Tokyo Press, 1978).

There have been moments when it was called over. In 1991 Sony launched hiring "with no credentials asked", in which applicants need not write the name of their university, and Shukan Post reported "we don't want deviation-score students any more". Yet the rate of going on to university (undergraduate) is at a record level, 57.1% in fiscal 2023, 58.6% in fiscal 2024 and 58.6% in fiscal 2025 (the School Basic Survey, on the formula revised in December 2025 and applied retrospectively), and the graduate has become, rather, the majority of the cohort.

The words change, but the sorting goes on. On 1 June 2015 an image was posted on Twitter claiming that the display on the application screen for Japan Post Bank's recruitment seminars switched between "full" and "places available" according to the university registered, and on 6 December 2021 Mynavi apologised after sending students in error an email whose subject line read "Daitoa and below" (both companies deny that any credential filter exists). What the phrase "credential filter" shows is not that credentials have stopped being everything, but that the judgment is now made quietly at the door.

made.label: 1960s "Credential society"
made.fact: The Heibonsha World Encyclopedia (revised edition) says the term gakureki shakai, "credential society", "came into wide use in Japan from around the start of the 1960s", and Nipponica too says "the name settled in in the 1960s". Johan Galtung, a member of the OECD education mission that came to Japan in January 1970, diagnosed that in Japan the rest of one's life is decided by an entrance examination on a single day at 18. The chief works of criticism are Makoto Aso and Morikazu Ushiogi, eds., On the Utility of Credentials: The Road from a Credential Society to an Ability Society (Yuhikaku, February 1977), Morikazu Ushiogi's The Turn of the Credential Society (University of Tokyo Press, January 1978), and Ronald Dore's The Diploma Disease (Iwanami Shoten, 1978).

keyfacts.text: The term gakureki shakai came into wide use in Japan from around the start of the 1960s (Heibonsha World Encyclopedia). Criticism of the credential society began in earnest from the 1960s, as the examination race grew fierce, its main themes being "credentials as a new status order" and "the reproduction of class".

Makoto Aso and Morikazu Ushiogi, eds., On the Utility of Credentials: The Road from a Credential Society to an Ability Society, was published by Yuhikaku in February 1977, and Morikazu Ushiogi's The Turn of the Credential Society by the University of Tokyo Press in January 1978.

In 1991 Sony launched hiring "with no credentials asked", not requiring the name of the university on the application, and Shukan Post of 3 May 1991 reported "the hiring revolution Sony has carried through: we don't want deviation-score students any more". Among those joining in 1992, the first intake, the Sankin Koryu group went from none the year before to five, and the Nittokomasen group rose by four.

The rate of going on to university (undergraduate), including those who left upper secondary school in earlier years, was 57.7% in fiscal 2023 and 59.1% in fiscal 2024 (up 1.4 points on the year, a record; final figures of 18 December 2024). The rate for universities and junior colleges together is 62.3%.

1 June 2015: the "full / places available" question on Japan Post Bank's seminar application screen. 6 December 2021: Mynavi's email in error reading "Daitoa and below". Both companies denied that any credential filter existed. There is no instance of "credential filter" in the record of Diet proceedings (as at September 2026).
